http_semantics.note: No business error code at all: the semantically unsatisfiable client filter is accepted as HTTP 200 plain success with a FULL (wrong) result set. Stronger than the 2xx+business-code pattern - silent 2xx success on semantically invalid input. No 400/422 rejection occurred (source confirms no request-level validation exists for min_count vs conditions length).

In this sense, should is equivalent to the operator OR.' [source, in-tree doc comment v1.18.0 lib/segment/src/index/query_estimator.rs:156-160] 'Estimate cardinality for min_should (at least min_count conditions). Returns zero immediately when min_count exceeds the number of estimations, which matches filter semantics and avoids generating impossible combinations.' [source, v1.19.0 lib/segment/src/index/query_optimization/optimized_filter.rs check()] 'Not enough conditions to match min_count -> return Ok(false)'.
contract_grounding.note: violates=True rationale: min_count=1 means 'at least 1 of the listed conditions must match'; with zero listed conditions this is unsatisfiable, so the clause must be false for every point (generalization of the documented should='at least one' semantics). Observed: all 10/10 points returned with 200 on count/scroll/query. The codebase itself asserts this semantics three independent ways in v1.18.0 (estimator exact(0) 'matches filter semantics'; exact checker check_min_should false; live doc should semantics), and v1.19.0 rewrote the optimized path to return Ok(false) for this exact edge - so the value is NOT compliant and the constraint domain is the right one.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST Filter deserialized as types.rs Filter{min_should:Option<MinShould>} -> StructPayloadIndex::optimize_filter (optimizer.rs:59-79): '&& !conditions.is_empty()' guard drops empty-conditions min_should to None regardless of min_count -> OptimizedFilter with all four clauses None -> check_optimized_filter (optimized_filter.rs:27-32, each None=>true) matches EVERY point -> executed by iter_filtered_points full-scan branch (struct_payload_index.rs:665-684, via struct_filtered_context 373-388) which serves scroll/count/query (query_points 584-607). Schema layer: MinShould derives Validate but only nested-validates conditions; no rule that min_count <= conditions.len(), so no 400 rejection possible. Contradicting in-tree paths that evaluate the edge correctly (unsatisfiable => no match): (a) exact checker query_checker.rs:56-75 '.filter(check).take(min_count).count()==min_count' gives 0==1 => false; (b) cardinality estimator query_estimator.rs:161-169 returns exact(0) with comment 'matches filter semantics'; (c) upstream v1.19.0 rewrite (read_view/optimizer.rs:48-110 + new OptimizedFilter::check) explicitly returns Ok(false) 'Not enough conditions to match min_count' for empty conditions with min_count>=1. The v1.18.0 optimizer path is the odd one out and was changed in v1.19.0.

mundane_explanation.surviving: undocumented-feature edge: min_should has zero prose documentation (live docs and v1.18-era extraction both 0 mentions), so a defender could argue 'empty conditions' is undefined behavior outside any published contract rather than a violation. Counter-evidence recorded for the auditor: v1.18.0's own estimator comment declares min_count>len => 0 'matches filter semantics'; v1.18.0's own exact checker evaluates it false; v1.19.0 changed the optimized path to match-none with an explicit code comment. Also the codebase's uniform optimizer convention of ignoring empty condition lists (should/must/must_not get the same is_empty guard) could be cited as by-design pattern - but for min_count>0 that convention contradicts the three in-tree semantics statements above.
